title: Demystifying a CXL Type-2 Device: A Heterogeneous Cooperative Computing Perspective
problem: CXL Type-2 devices are newly commercially available but their performance characteristics across three key memory access types (cache-coherent device-to-host, device-to-device, and host CPU-to-device) are not well understood. There is a need to characterize their latency and bandwidth to identify suitable applications.
motivation: Understanding CXL Type-2 device capabilities is essential for identifying and optimizing applications that can exploit their unique heterogeneous computing features.
method: The researchers tested real CXL Type-2 devices using microbenchmarks—small programs that measure speed and data-transfer rates across three different memory access paths—and compared them against simulated versions and other technologies (emulated CXL Type-2, CXL Type-3, and PCIe). They then adapted two Linux memory-optimization features—zswap (which compresses data in RAM) and ksm (which merges duplicate data)—to use CXL for device-to-host communication and evaluated them on Redis to demonstrate real-world benefits.
key_novelty: CXL Type-2 devices eliminate most of the performance slowdown that memory-optimization features add—reducing overhead from 4.5-10.3 times down to nearly zero—by enabling direct, fast communication between the device and host instead of going through the CPU or older PCIe connections.
contributions: Comprehensive characterization of CXL Type-2 device latency and bandwidth for cache-coherent and non-coherent memory accesses
Comparative performance analysis with emulated CXL Type-2, CXL Type-3, and PCIe-based systems
CXL-based implementations of Linux memory optimization features (zswap and ksm)
Demonstration that CXL-based optimizations achieve near-zero tail latency increase in Redis versus 4.5-10.3× with CPU-based approaches

metrics.speedup: Tail latency: practically 0× with CXL-based zswap/ksm vs 4.5-10.3× with CPU-based and up to 8.1× with PCIe-based approaches
metrics.other: Latency and bandwidth characterization across memory access types

limitations: Evaluation scope and generalization of results to other applications beyond Redis not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: CXL Type-2 device characterization and optimization for memory management
